scenarios.name: Counter-Strafe Drill
scenarios.short: Strafe, stop, one-tap the head before the window closes.
scenarios.desc: An enemy appears while you are strafing at full speed. Release the movement key or counter-strafe, then tap the head before the window closes. Shots fired above the rifle's movement accuracy threshold have more spread and cost points.
tips: Watch the speed meter. Shots only count as accurate once the bar turns green, about 0.1 s after you stop pressing.
In StrafeLab, releasing the key crosses the threshold in about 106 ms, and counter-strafing takes about 100 ms.
If you counter-strafe, tap the opposite key. Holding it accelerates you the other way.

scenarios.name: ADAD Strafe Shooting
scenarios.short: Keep strafing and land shots at the dead point of each strafe.
scenarios.desc: Shooting while strafing in Valorant means firing at the instant your velocity crosses zero between A and D. Keep moving: if you stand still the drill warns you and your hits score less. Hits at the peak of a strafe score full points, and lucky hits while moving score almost nothing.
tips: The speed bar briefly turns green as your strafe reverses. Shoot during that window.
A short release before reversing (A, release, shoot, D) is easier than pure ADAD.
Keep the crosshair at head height the whole time so you only have to time the shot.

scenarios.name: Strafing Bots: Rifle Taps
scenarios.short: Tap the heads of bots that ADAD, crouch and stutter like real players.
scenarios.desc: Humanoid bots with head, body and leg hitboxes strafe unpredictably, using the same acceleration and stopping as you do. A rifle headshot kills in one tap (160 damage) and body shots take four. This trains following and timing strafing heads.
tips: Fire when the bot reverses direction, because that's when its head stops.
Tap or burst. Spraying climbs out of the head fast.
Track with small corrections instead of chasing big swings.

scenarios.name: Micro Adjust
scenarios.short: Tiny head-sized targets a few degrees away. Precision over speed.
scenarios.desc: Small head-sized targets spawn 1 to 6 degrees from the last one, which is the distance of a correction after your crosshair placement is slightly off. Misses cost points, so precision matters more than raw speed.
tips: Move with your fingers and wrist, not your arm.
Don't click until the crosshair has settled on the target.
Grip lightly. A tense hand overshoots small corrections.

scenarios.name: Macro Flicks
scenarios.short: Wide flicks of 30 to 150 degrees. Tracks overshoot and undershoot.
scenarios.desc: Targets spawn far to your side, like an enemy appearing off-angle or a teammate calling a flank. Every flick is analysed: clean, overshoot (you passed the target) or undershoot (you stopped short and corrected). Use the ratio to tune your sensitivity and arm movement.
tips: Mostly overshooting usually means tension or a sensitivity that's too high for you.
Mostly undershooting means you're hesitating. Commit to the flick.
One big arm movement and one small wrist correction. No more.

scenarios.name: Grid Taps
scenarios.short: Tap four targets across a five-by-three grid.
scenarios.desc: Four targets stay active on a five-by-three wall grid. A hit lights an empty cell and adds 100 points. Misses cost 25 points and reset your streak.
tips: Find the next target while finishing your current flick.
Try to keep a long streak as you increase your pace.

scenarios.name: Multi-Target Switch
scenarios.short: Switch between targets at different depths before they expire.
scenarios.desc: Four lanes spawn targets at different heights and depths. Targets brighten before they expire. Each hit earns 100 points, each miss costs 25, and an expired target costs 15.
tips: Prioritize the targets that are starting to brighten.
Lead with your eyes as you switch between near and far targets.

scenarios.name: Strafe Tracking
scenarios.short: Follow a strafing bot and score for time on target.
scenarios.desc: Keep your crosshair on a bot as it strafes, pauses, and crouches at higher difficulties. You earn 100 points per second on target and get a separate reading for time on the head.
tips: Follow the bot with your crosshair. There is no shot to fire.
Start with the torso and work up to the head as your tracking steadies.

scenarios.name: Sniper: Strafing Targets
scenarios.short: Bolt-action scoped rifle vs ADAD strafers and doorway crossers.
scenarios.desc: A heavy bolt-action sniper with 2.5x and 5x zoom (right-click cycles). Body shots kill and legs do not. Bots strafe at mid range or sprint across doorway gaps at long range. Unscoped and moving shots are wildly inaccurate, so stop, scope and click.
tips: Against strafers, aim where the bot reverses and fire as it stops.
Against crossers, pre-aim the doorway and fire as the body enters, not when you see it.
The rifle unscopes after every shot, so re-scope with right-click.
Scoped sensitivity follows Valorant's Scoped Sensitivity Multiplier (Settings).

scenarios.name: Reaction Time
scenarios.short: Click the instant the panel turns green. Hard adds blue decoys.
scenarios.desc: This is a pure visual reaction test over 12 trials. False starts and clicking a blue decoy each add a 25 ms penalty to your average. Hard mode adds go/no-go decoys, which train you not to shoot teammates or bait utility.
tips: Stay relaxed with your finger resting on the button.
Look at the centre of the panel, not the edges.
Your monitor and mouse latency are included, the same as in a real game.

scenarios.name: Angle Hold
scenarios.short: Hold a doorway. Kill swingers before their reaction timer fires.
scenarios.desc: You hold the angle while enemies swing out from behind the walls, stop and shoot back after their reaction time. Kill them first. Wide swingers sprint through and jigglers bait your shot. Good crosshair placement at the wall edge and head height is what wins this.
tips: Keep your crosshair on the edge of the wall at head height.
Let wide swingers run into your crosshair instead of chasing them.
Don't shoot jiggle peeks that won't stop. Wait for a committed swing.

scenarios.name: Peek Duels
scenarios.short: 10 rounds: swing off cover, stop, kill, without dying.
scenarios.desc: This is a game-like 1v1 peek simulation. Enemies hold angles you can't see from behind your cover. Peek, find them, stop and kill them before they out-trade you. Enemies react after a reaction time, then fire rifle taps at your 150 HP: they hit you less while you're moving or in the air, and a headshot is 160 damage. Every second you're exposed counts against you, and fast clean peeks score the most.
tips: Swing wide and fast, then stop into the shot. Being exposed while standing still is when they hit you most.
Moving makes you harder to hit, but you can't shoot back accurately until you've stopped (about 0.1 s).
Clear one side at a time. Peeking both sides at once exposes you to two angles.

scenarios.name: Air Strafe Course
scenarios.short: Time trial over gaps. Curve mid-air around walls to land.
scenarios.desc: A platform time trial with the knife out. Run before take-off to carry speed into the jump. Some landings sit behind walls and can only be reached by curving mid-air. Hold the strafe key in the direction you turn the mouse to bend your path.
tips: To curve right, hold D and sweep the mouse right smoothly. Don't hold W.
Before a curve, run along the orange stripe (the inside line) and jump at the very edge.
Turning fast doesn't cost speed, but your path can only bend so quickly, so start the turn as soon as you clear the wall.
Falling sends you back to the last checkpoint with a +2s penalty.

scenarios.name: Silent Jumps
scenarios.short: Crouch-jump onto ledges and land without making a sound.
scenarios.desc: Six ledges that a normal jump can't reach, all inside a sound zone. Hold Walk (or Crouch) the whole way: a jump is only silent while Walk or Crouch is held, and walking speed also keeps your landings quiet. Crouch-jump onto each ledge: crouching in the air pulls your legs up so your feet clear the edge, and because you land near the top of your jump the landing is silent too. Walk down the steps on the far side, since a small drop at walking speed is silent. Every footstep, jump or landing that would be heard costs +2s.
tips: Keep Walk or Crouch held when you press jump. Jumping with neither is always heard, even when standing still.
Walk or Crouch silences the jump even straight out of a run, but you'd still be moving fast, and a fast landing is heard.
Approach at walking speed. A landing while moving faster than a walk is loud even if the drop is tiny.
Press crouch as you jump (or crouch first, then jump). Crouching late, after the top of your jump, may not clear the ledge.
You can release crouch before you touch down and still land silently. What matters is how far you fall, not your stance.
Don't jump down from a ledge. A full drop is always heard, so take the steps.

scenarios.name: Movement Course
scenarios.short: Silent walk zones, crouch vents, box climbs, a shooting gate and a held room.
scenarios.desc: A time trial that mixes the movement you use in real rounds. Walk silently through the sound zone and crouch-jump its ledge without being heard (each running footstep, jump without Walk, or loud landing costs +1s), crouch through the vent, climb boxes, counter-strafe to clear the shooting gallery that opens the gate, then clear a held room without getting traded.
tips: Hold Shift in the purple zone. Walking makes no footstep sound.
Hold crouch before you reach the vent so you don't bump the ceiling.
In the gallery, stop fully before every shot. Moving shots miss.
Peek the final room with a quick swing. Every 0.45s you're exposed adds +2s.
